title: Signed Average Effect Inference When Effect and Label Reliability Vanish Together
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4; salvageable=false. The checked result is mathematically sound at its narrow benchmark scope, but field-tier upgrade requires a new broad frontier program.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope.

The note proves its four-coordinate Gaussian limit and a strict connected-interval improvement, but only inside a known-variance, homoskedastic Gaussian location model with independent symmetric coding error.
Attainment in the original experiment is supplied through existential randomized Le Cam reconstruction kernels rather than an executable finite-sample procedure with quantified coverage error.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the four-coordinate Gaussian limit and a strict connected-interval information gain. An independent replay of the outward-rounded positive-reliability certificate passed with a strict gap exceeding 0.0015993 and six certified cells. The field-tier claim collapsed at D0.5: a broad validation frontier and directly computable finite-sample intervals would require a new research program. The unused Agostini-Amendola-Ranestad citation and duplicate positive-reliability theorem remain editorial cleanup items.
tldr: When the randomized treatment effect and code reliability both vanish at rate \(n^{-1/4}\), with \(m_n\asymp\sqrt n\) gold labels, the experiment converges uniformly to a four-coordinate Gaussian observation.  Sharp signed-effect risk and uniformly honest connected-interval length are characterized by certified endpoint programs.  At the preregistered benchmark \(H=2\), \(D=1\), \(c=1\), and \(\alpha=0.05\), a reproducible direct certificate at reliability \(d=0.1\) gives \(L_G(0,0.1)\leq3.44375<3.44530\leq L_{-}(0,0.1)\), with explicit data-based connected kernels and a partition-certified positive-reliability region.
gap: Singular mixture theory supplies the quadratic score, regular misclassification theory supplies validation estimators, and optimal confidence-set theory supplies inclusion-test duality; none resolves connected signed-effect intervals in their joint weak-code boundary experiment.
fill: A compact-uniform experiment theorem, sharp endpoint decision program, finite primal--dual certificates, data-based attaining rules, and a strict-information region establish the full frontier without attributing the known quadratic score to this project.
